items.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: Even classical composers did this all the time. Even Bach, Mozart, Chopin — you can find instances of major sevenths against dominant seventh chords.

ctx.x: There is no such thing as a wrong note. And I mean, well, let’s see, in relation to — well one of the most basic things is people say don’t play a major seventh on a dominant seventh chord. But if you play this [plays piano] it sounds pretty good to me. But what happens most of the time is that an inexperienced player will play that note [plays piano] and then just move away from it because they didn’t really hear what that note implied. Really, improvising music is exactly like using a language. So using notes…
Let me backtrack just a second though. If you said this is not something that has a place in academia, isn’t the whole —
